role.altitude: She still grades each batch by look, smell and a meter reading, and she still accepts a recipe only after she checks it and tastes a trial. She stops hunting a paper rule for limits and retyping percentages and allergen rows when the stored specs are complete. She does not gain a right to let a list set the grade, or to let a calculated table stand as the recipe.
skills_to_grow: Read the paper grade rule when the limit row is blank
Compute percentages and allergen rows by hand when an ingredient spec is missing
role.ambitious_version: She still grades and she still tastes. A blank limit row stays a paper check. An unaccepted calculation is not the recipe. A trial batch that fails does not become the formula.

tasks.short: Grade products by type, color, bouquet and moisture.

steps.what: List stored limits for type, color, bouquet and moisture content.
Judge type, color and bouquet on the batch in person.
Read the moisture content on the meter for this batch.
Decide the grade under the government regulations or the workplace rule.
Write that grade on the batch record herself.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store lists the stored limits for type, color, bouquet and moisture content before she looks at the batch. She still judges the batch, reads the meter, decides the grade and writes it on the batch record. The list does not grade the batch, does not raise an out-of-range alert, does not send the grade, and does not fill the batch record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The limits for type, color, bouquet and moisture sat on a paper rule, so each batch started with a search.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored row can list those limits for a product the quality lead has already specified.
tasks.still_hard: Color, bouquet and the meter reading are on the batch in front of her, not in the row.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person who can say this batch matches the grade. A list cannot see or smell it.
tasks.altitude: Her week still spends most of its time on the batch. She no longer hunts the written limits when the row exists. She does not gain a right to let the list set the grade.

reach.task: Keep the grade limit row for each product
reach.learn: Which line of the rule sets the moisture band

evidence.claim: Grade limits are workplace specs or product rules. Which rule applies is not decided here, and a stored row does not replace her look at the batch. Model knowledge.

The range is a scenario, not a measured saving. A week with a complete limit row drops only the search. A week with a blank row saves nothing. Looking, measuring, deciding and writing stay. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The grade limit row fields are product type, color band, bouquet note, moisture minimum, moisture maximum, and the regulation or workplace rule name. The quality lead maintains that row in {DOCS} outside this task, and that upkeep is not counted here.
If any of those fields is blank, the list returns nothing. She reads the paper rule while she decides the grade, and that decision stays at full time.
The batch color, bouquet and moisture are not stored before she looks. She reads the meter herself in this task. No sensor writes the moisture, and the list does not contain this batch's reading.
The list does not grade, does not raise an alert, does not send the grade, and does not fill the batch record. She writes the grade herself.
Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is her share of telling the quality lead when a limit row is wrong. The design keeps no staff score and no personal data.
unknowns: Whether this plant keeps grade limits as a maintained table.
Which products are graded to a government rule rather than a workplace rule.
research_questions: For a sample of batches last month, how often was the grade limit already written down before she started?

incremental.description: Tell the quality lead when a grade limit row is wrong so the next list is current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a week of products with no stored limit row, so she still opens the paper rule and nothing is saved. High is a week where every product has a complete limit row: only the search goes, and looking, measuring, deciding and writing stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Formulate or modify recipes for specific food products.

steps.what: Read the current recipes for these specific kinds of products.
Decide how to modify these recipes.
Draft one way to formulate these recipes.

loop.input: The kind of product, the change she decided, and the current ingredient names.
loop.output: One proposed ingredient list with rough amounts.
loop.check: At the acceptance step she reads whether the proposal is the kind of product and the change she named, not whether an id matches.
loop.stop: One proposal, or no proposal if the current recipe or the named change is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot propose a new formulation from a free-text change.

steps.what: Fill calculated recipe v1 for these products from ingredient specs only.
Check the calculated recipes still mean those products.
Write the recipes she accepts, or correct them by hand.
Mix and taste a trial batch of these recipes.

tasks.design: A bounded draft in the {DOCS} recipe file proposes one formulation, and a separate fill step writes calculated recipe v1 from stored ingredient specs only. She must accept that exact version, then she writes the recipe she keeps and mixes and tastes a trial batch. The draft does not write the recipe; the fill does not file it as live, does not raise an alert, and does not send it.
tasks.previous_blocker: A new variant started from a blank page, and percentages, cost and allergen rows were copied off ingredient cards by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose one variant, and arithmetic can total percentages, cost and allergen rows from stored specs.
tasks.still_hard: The trial batch and the taste decide whether the line can make it. A missing allergen flag stops the fill.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether this plant can make the variant, and she is the one who tastes it.
tasks.altitude: She still decides the change, accepts or rewrites the recipe, and tastes the trial. The draft and the fill remove retyping when specs are complete. She does not gain a right to let calculated recipe v1 stand unaccepted.

reach.task: Keep allergen flags and cost on each ingredient spec
reach.learn: Which flag must be present before a recipe can be used

evidence.claim: Red Rabbit's nextfood.ai drafts formulations from a development brief. The same announcement gives a vendor time claim with no customer named; this task does not use that figure.
Aptean Bakery ERP keeps formulas, flags allergens and shows cost per product. This task's fill is arithmetic from stored specs, not a claim that the plant uses that product.
A new recipe must update the allergen information on loose goods. In 2021 the NVWA inspected 1,910 artisan producers (bakeries, ice cream shops, butchers) and about half did not comply.
No Annex III area applies. Article 50 transparency applies from 2 August 2026 if customers meet a chatbot or generated content.

The range is a scenario, not a measured saving. A week with complete ingredient specs drops only the draft and the fill. A week with a missing spec saves nothing. Deciding, checking, writing and tasting stay. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Ingredient spec fields are ingredient name, cost per kilogram, and allergen flags. The quality lead maintains them in {DOCS} outside this task, and that work is not counted. Cost is a field on that spec, not a live pull from the finance system.
If a cost or an allergen flag is missing, the fill does not run. She calculates by hand in the write step, which stays at full time.
The draft sees only the current ingredient names and the change she named. It does not see cost or allergen flags, and it does not send the recipe to an external model or to a customer.
Calculated recipe v1 is not the live recipe. Her check accepts that exact version. Any later change voids the approval, and the recipe she writes by hand is the one she trials.
The fill does not update a customer label, does not raise an alert, and does not send a cost anywhere. The draft does not write the recipe.
Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours keeps the draft instruction aligned with the spec fields. The design keeps no score of her corrections.
unknowns: Whether ingredient specs already carry cost and allergen flags.
Who may sign a recipe before it is used on the line.
research_questions: For the last recipes she changed, were allergen flags present on every ingredient before she started?

incremental.description: Keep the draft instruction aligned with the current ingredient spec fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a week of recipe changes where an ingredient spec is missing, so the fill does not run and she calculates by hand. High is a week where every spec is complete and she still decides, checks, writes and tastes the trial. A vendor time claim is not used. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
